name: Micky's Unannounced Visit
description: Micky arrives at Laurie's home and knocks on the door. Jimmy, Laurie's husband, answers and greets him quietly, seeming uneasy. Micky says he just wants to say hello to his daughter, Kasie. Laurie approaches and questions why he is there, pointing out it is not his scheduled visitation day. Micky explains he won’t be available next weekend because he has a fight. He turns to Jimmy, asking him to help, since he can’t talk to Laurie. Jimmy calls Kasie to the door. She runs up, hugs her father, and says hello. Laurie curses under her breath, frustrated with Jimmy. Kasie stands in the doorway as Micky tells her about his upcoming fight with Saoul Mamby and says he’ll start making good money soon. He promises to move to a bigger apartment so she can stay with him more often. Laurie scoffs, calling the idea laughable and accusing Micky of misleading their daughter. She closes the door, and voices argue inside. Kasie shouts through the door, 'Good luck, Daddy!' Micky calls back, 'Thanks, Kasie.'

name: Dicky Interrupts the Encounter with a Fake Police Stop
description: A beat-up station wagon pulls into the area behind the Volvo, its bright headlights shining. Dicky steps into view, holding a cheap megaphone, his voice slurred as he orders the businessman to get out of the car and place his hands on the roof. The businessman complies, nervous, his pants still undone, hands raised. Dicky stands in silhouette against the glare, holding up a wallet like a badge. He demands the man empty his pockets—ID, wallet, cash—onto the roof of the car. As the man obeys, Dicky asks if his wife knows he’s there. Confused, the businessman starts to turn, questioning whether Dicky is a real officer. Dicky shouts at him not to turn around and to keep following orders. The man walks to the sidewalk as Dicky takes the cash and mutters to Karen to take half and get them some rocks. Before anything else happens, the sound of a police siren cuts through the night. A cop car arrives, and a bald businessman jumps out, pointing at Dicky. 'That's the guy, he got me and he's doin' it again!' Little Dicky walks in, and she quickly wipes her eyes, telling him to go back upstairs. She dials the phone. Micky answers, standing in his apartment above the garage, his eyes fixed on the same HBO broadcast. He listens as Alice speaks, her voice trembling with anger and disbelief. name: Dicky Smokes Crack on Camera and Dreams of Redemption
description: In a filthy kitchen lit by flickering overhead light, Dicky leans against a broken dining table, a crack pipe in hand. The HBO crew films as he lights the pipe and inhales, his words tumbling out fast and slurred. He talks about his boxing career, about fighting Sugar Ray too soon, about the money he could have made if things had gone differently. He speaks of his daughter Kerry, saying he wants her to be proud of him. Karen watches from nearby, asking why he lets them film him smoking, what the movie is even about. The HBO producer says it’s to show what crack addiction really looks like, for kids to see the truth. BooBoo steps in, trying to explain how crack affects the brain, but Dicky cuts him off, waving the pipe. He says it’s his story, and showing this moment will make his and Micky’s comeback more powerful. He takes another hit. As the high hits, Dicky drifts. He sees himself dancing slowly across the room, loose and smiling, caught in a quiet rhythm. He sits by a window, calm. He and Karen kiss on the couch, lost in each other. These moments flicker like film strips, then snap apart at the sound of a phone off the hook. Dicky jerks back, eyes wide, smoke curling from his lips. He exhales and mutters that he needs to find money for Micky, now.

name: Dicky Returns to the Gym
description: Dicky walks back into the gym as Micky is about to begin working out with O'Keefe. Alice asks what happened, and Dicky says O'Keefe told him he can't train with Micky. Alice protests, insisting Dicky was essential to Micky's victory over Sanchez. Alice challenges them to ask Micky whether he could have beaten Sanchez without Dicky. All eyes turn to Micky, who hesitates before saying he wouldn't have won without Dicky—he used what he learned from him in the fight. He adds that he also needed O'Keefe, Sal, and his family. Charlene grows angry, claiming they gave Micky focus and confidence, while Alice insists Dicky saved him. Charlene calls Dicky a junkie, and Dicky fires back that he's eight months sober and points out that O'Keefe, like him, is in recovery—so why is O'Keefe allowed to stay and not him? Micky declares he's the one fighting and knows what he needs. Charlene shrieks that he can't choose Dicky over them. Micky says he wants Dicky back, and he wants Charlene, O'Keefe, and his family too. Charlene tells him he sounds like the people they've always fought against, then turns and walks out. O'Keefe follows, glancing back sadly at Micky. Alice comforts Micky, saying everything happens for a reason. Art Ramalho helps Dicky put on gloves, headgear, and mouthguard while another boxer gears up Micky. Ray Ramalho announces Dicky Ecklund as the pride of Lowell, which unsettles Micky. Dicky says he’s been training in jail and is ready. The brothers begin to spar, quickly falling into rhythm—Dicky lands a sharp combination, Micky responds with hard body shots, they grapple, tie up, break, and continue exchanging blows around the ring.

name: Micky Wakes Up in Pain and Hesitates to Call Charlene
description: Micky lies asleep on the couch in his apartment, still dressed in his clothes from the previous day, bandages wrapped around his head. The TV flickers in the dim room. He stirs, sits up, and moves into the small kitchen, where he takes a beer from the refrigerator and swallows pain medication. He picks up a cocktail napkin with Charlene’s number and a heart drawn on it, then walks to the phone. He begins to dial, stops, stares at the number, and hangs up. He returns to the couch, lies down, and falls back asleep as the TV continues to play.

description: Charlene stands on the doorstep of Micky's apartment and knocks on the door. From inside, Micky stirs, gets up from the couch, and peers through the shade. He sees her and crouches out of sight. Charlene calls out that she saw his shadow and heard him speak. She demands he open the door and tell her why he didn’t call her the day before. Micky remains still, then finally walks to the door and opens it. Charlene, seeing his bandaged face, reacts with surprise.

name: Charlene Re-Bands Micky's Face and Asks Him Out
description: Charlene stands on Micky's doorstep, knocking until he answers. She tells him she saw his shadow and heard him speak, demanding to know why he didn’t call her the day before. When he opens the door, she notices the bandage peeling from his face. She steps inside and leads him to the bathroom, where she carefully removes the old bandage and re-wraps his wounds. As she works, they talk—Micky says he fought someone who wasn’t ready, someone who didn’t stand a chance. Charlene tells him about her past, about leaving home at sixteen. The moment settles into quiet closeness. When she’s done, she asks if he wants to go to dinner and a movie. He looks at her, silent for a beat, then nods.

name: Micky Faces Stares at Dunkin' Donuts
description: Micky pushes into a crowded Dunkin' Donuts on a rainy day, exhausted, his hand swollen and clenched. People turn to look, some whispering as he moves through the room. He spots Mickey O'Keefe in the back, still in his police uniform, sipping coffee and reading the paper. Micky calls out and O'Keefe stands, greeting him with a hug. O'Keefe eyes his hand. 'Looks bettah,' he says. Micky says it's getting there. O'Keefe tells him to come down to the gym, then laughs. 'Ya fat fuck, look atcha.' Micky glances around at the onlookers. 'Now I gotta worry about this movie tonight on HBO,' he says. 'Everybody lookin' at me like I did somethin' wrong. Ain't my fault he's on TV.' O'Keefe shakes his head. 'It's bettah for ya if ya don't see it, Micky. It's just gonna make ya feel bad.' He turns to the others. 'What are you lookin' at? He ain't gonna be on TV. It's his crazy brothah.' The room falls quiet, eyes still fixed on them.

name: Dicky Plays With Son and Discusses Documentary During Prison Visit
description: Dicky sits across from his mother Alice in the crowded visitor's room at Billerica House of Corrections, playing with his four-year-old son. He laughs as he pretends to be hit in the mouth, popping out his fake teeth after the boy playfully punches him. The child bursts into laughter, and Dicky joins in, pretending his teeth have been knocked out. Alice, smoking a Lucky Strike with three newspapers in her lap, tells Dicky people are talking about the 'High on Crack Street' documentary airing that night. She says it’s making him and the city look bad. Dicky puts his teeth back in and says it wasn’t supposed to turn out this way, adding they did it for the kids. He asks if Micky will watch it, then wonders why Micky hasn’t come to visit. He tells Alice that all he thinks about in prison is getting out, working with Micky again, and getting a second chance to win a title. A guard calls out that the visit is ending in five minutes. The boy reaches forward and gently cups his father’s nose as the moment quiets.

He laughs, performs for the others, shadowboxing and playing to the crowd. The mood shifts when footage shows his young son crying at his arrest. Dicky stops moving. He stares at the screen, then lowers his head, tears running down his face.

name: Silence After the Movie
description: Micky and Charlene walk out of the theater without speaking. Charlene breaks the silence, asking why Micky wanted to see a movie with no sex and wonders aloud which Lowell guy on a road crew recommended it in Lexington. Micky hurries ahead to the car, patting his pockets for his keys, muttering that he must have left them in the theater, calling himself a dummy. Charlene calls his name and tells him the keys are in his hand. He looks down and sees them clenched in his fist. At the 1989 silver Ford Tempo, Charlene watches him as he starts the car. As he begins to back out, she asks what’s going on, suggesting he’s avoiding a girlfriend. She presses, saying that must be why he took her to Lexington. Micky stops the car, shifts into park, and turns off the engine. He tells her he doesn’t have a girlfriend and says he came to Lexington because he didn’t want to be seen in Lowell. Charlene asks what he’s ashamed of. Micky says he told everyone he’d win the fight and get back on track, and he promised Kasie they’d get a bigger place so she could move in. Charlene reminds him he said he never should have fought that opponent, but his mother and brother wanted him to. Micky snaps that it doesn’t matter—he was alone in the ring. Charlene asks if he really thinks his family is looking out for him. Micky turns to her and says she can’t talk about his family like that. She holds his gaze and tells him to look at himself. He leans in and kisses her. The kiss grows more intense, lasting a moment before they pull apart.

name: Dicky's Withdrawal in Prison
description: Dicky is alone in his cell at the Billerica House of Corrections, writhing in pain as he goes through crack withdrawal. He trembles violently, sweat soaking his clothes, his breath coming in ragged gasps. He screams into the empty space, clutching his head, eyes wide with hallucinations. He bangs his fists against the wall, then drags his nails across his arms, breaking the skin. Over hours that stretch into days, the fits come and go—shivering, pacing, collapsing onto the bunk, then jerking upright again in panic. His voice grows hoarse from shouting. Finally, he lies motionless on the floor, pale and drained, breathing slowly. The storm has passed. He doesn't move, but his eyes are clear.

Micky and Neary meet in the middle, trading punches without backing down. Neary lands a hard right to Micky's temple, wobbling him, then drives him to the ropes with a barrage of blows. He focuses on Micky's body, following with sharp uppercuts, trying to finish him. Micky, pinned, begins to fire back, absorbing the punishment as Dicky shouts from the corner. Micky slips off the ropes, raises his gloves, and signals he's still in the fight. He steps forward and lands a clean left hook, then a powerful left uppercut that snaps Neary's head back. Another left hook to the body and a huge uppercut rock Neary, shifting the momentum in the round.

As he reaches the door, Dicky calls after him with one final warning. Micky pauses, then leaves, his face showing the weight of Dicky’s words.
